text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Former combatants marched to the office of Prime Minister Hage Geingob to once again protest over their struggle to find work in post independent Namibia.
- Geingob has vowed to ensure that a future two-term limit on the presidency is enshrined in the constitution.
- Claims by an environmental group that the planned Epupa hydro-electric project will be a "white elephant and a financial disaster" have been dismissed by power utility Nampower.
- The buildings of the national council are to be further extended at a cost of N$20 million because there is not enough office space for administrative personnel.
- Residents of Mariental, in the south of the country, are expected to protest on Wednesday over what they say is "discriminatory actions by the police".
